# bob attachments

Copy files into the vault and show where copies came from

```text title="bob attachments --help"
Copy files into the vault and show where copies came from

Bare `bob attachments` prints this help. import copies files in; origin reports where a copy came from.

Usage: bob attachments <COMMAND>

Commands:
  import  Copy image and file paths into the vault
  origin  Show where a vault attachment came from

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

Bare `bob attachments` prints this help: the group has no flag-only
read-only member.

Examples:
  bob attachments import ~/tmp/screenshots/x.png   Copy an image into img/
  bob attachments import -f json -- ~/tmp/a.png     Copy paths as JSON
  bob attachments origin img/x.png                  Show where img/x.png came from

See docs/attachments.md for the origin journal contract.
Run 'bob attachments <command> --help' for more information on a command.
```

## bob attachments import

Copy image and file paths into the vault

```text title="bob attachments import --help"
Copy one to ten explicit paths into the vault exactly as a `%c` clipboard line would: images land in `img/` (embedded at 400px), other files land in `file/`, an identical existing file is reused, and a name conflict gains an eight-character SHA-256 suffix. It never edits notes. Every copied attachment appends one `attachment.import` origin event to `.bob/attachments/<host>.jsonl` under `bob_sync.lock` (wait at most 3s); a failed append removes the files this import created.

Usage: bob attachments import [OPTIONS] <PATH>...

Arguments:
  <PATH>...
          Absolute image or file path to copy into the vault

Options:
  -b, --bob-dir <DIR>
          Bob vault root; defaults to BOB_DIR or ~/bob

  -f, --format <FORMAT>
          Output format: human or json

          [default: human]
          [possible values: human, json]

  -h, --help
          Show help

Examples:
  bob attachments import ~/tmp/screenshots/x.png
  bob attachments import -f json -- ~/tmp/a.png /tmp/b.pdf

Environment:
  BOB_DIR                   Bob vault root when --bob-dir is omitted
  BOB_VAULT_SYNC_LOCK_FILE  Maintenance lock; defaults to ${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR:-/tmp}/bob_sync.lock
  HOME                      Home directory for the ~ display form
  NO_COLOR                  Disable colored output

Exit codes:
  0  imported every path
  1  missing, not_a_file, not_absolute, too_many, lock_busy, or I/O failure
  2  usage error

See docs/attachments.md for the origin journal contract.
```

## bob attachments origin

Show where a vault attachment came from

```text title="bob attachments origin --help"
Show the recorded origin of one vault-relative attachment path. A renamed or deduped copy still resolves through its content hash; an edited copy resolves through its saved path. The lookup is read-only: it never writes the vault.

Usage: bob attachments origin [OPTIONS] <VAULT_PATH>

Arguments:
  <VAULT_PATH>
          Vault-relative attachment path, e.g. img/x.png

Options:
  -b, --bob-dir <DIR>
          Bob vault root; defaults to BOB_DIR or ~/bob

  -f, --format <FORMAT>
          Output format: human or json

          [default: human]
          [possible values: human, json]

  -h, --help
          Show help

Examples:
  bob attachments origin img/20261103_142837.png
  bob attachments origin -f json -- img/20261103_142837.png

Environment:
  BOB_DIR                   Bob vault root when --bob-dir is omitted
  NO_COLOR                  Disable colored output

Exit codes:
  0  resolved (including no recorded origin)
  1  not_found or I/O failure
  2  usage error

See docs/attachments.md for the origin journal contract.
```
